title: Fragile environment variable detection via env parsing
reasoning: The script attempts to detect if any environment variables starting with 'MAIL_ACCOUNT__' are set by parsing the output of the 'env' command. This approach is fragile because 'read' combined with 'env' output does not correctly handle environment values containing newlines. If a variable contains a newline followed by a string starting with 'MAIL_ACCOUNT__', the script will incorrectly conclude that an account is configured via environment variables. While this only affects the 'friendly' error message logic, it is less robust than using Bash's built-in variable prefix expansion.
reproduction: Run the script with an environment variable containing a newline that mimics the prefix, e.g., 'export SPOOF=$"foo\nMAIL_ACCOUNT__ANY=1"; scripts/run-streamable-http.sh'. The script will bypass the missing config check even if no real account variables exist.
recommendation: Use Bash's built-in indirect expansion to check for variables with a specific prefix: 'if [[ -n "${!MAIL_ACCOUNT__*}" ]]; then ACCOUNT_ENV_CONFIGURED="true"; fi'.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no tests provided for this shell script in the project.
suggestedRegressionTest: A test case that executes the script with a multiline environment variable that does not contain a real account configuration, verifying that the script still identifies the configuration as missing.
minimumFixScope: Replace the 'while' loop block (lines 60-65) with a single conditional using Bash prefix expansion.
